record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.context_brief: Direct proof of Bouchet's bipartite circle-graph corollary
record.original_question: Give a direct proof that graph complementation preserves circle graphs within bipartite graphs: if G is a bipartite graph and G is a circle graph, then the complement of G is also a circle graph. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle. The proof should avoid deriving this corollary through Naji's theorem about the solvability over GF(2) of the associated system S(G).

evidence.quote: Also in [9], Bouchet posed the following problem: Is there a direct proof of Corollary 42?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A circle graph is the intersection graph of a finite collection of chords of a circle: each vertex corresponds to a chord, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if the corresponding chords cross. A graph is bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two independent sets. The complement of a simple graph G = (V,E) is the graph on the same vertex set V whose edges are exactly the pairs of distinct vertices that are non-adjacent in G.

It is known that if G is a bipartite graph and G is a circle graph, then the complement of G is also a circle graph. One proof of this fact proceeds by invoking a theorem characterizing circle graphs as exactly those graphs whose associated linear system S(G) is solvable over the field GF(2) with two elements.

Problem: Provide a direct proof of the following statement that does not use the GF(2)-solvability characterization of circle graphs: for every bipartite graph G, if G is a circle graph then the complement of G is also a circle graph.
artifact.status_search_result: An elementary, direct proof avoiding Naji's GF(2)-system characterization was given by Louis Esperet and Matěj Stehlík in their 2020 paper "Bipartite complements of circle graphs" (arXiv:1910.08388), published in Discrete Mathematics. Their proof is geometric and does not rely on Naji's theorem.

status_evidence.snippet: Bouchet asked whether Theorem 1 has an elementary proof. We provide such a proof.
status_evidence.claim: Esperet and Stehlík gave a direct/elementary proof avoiding Naji's theorem.
